headline: India: Over 50 killed as Houthis target Yemen military camp with ballistic missiles
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- India: Over 50 killed as Houthis target Yemen military camp with ballistic missiles.
- South Asia: UN agency to end monthly aid to 500,000 people in Gaza over funding shortfall.
- Africa: Sudan: Drone Strikes Kill Civilians in Darfur and Kordofan As Attacks Target Eastern Sudan.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army acquisition command awards contracts worth $6.8B in 2026.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: US Army acquisition command awards contracts worth $6.8B in 2026.
The Mission and Installation Contracting Command awarded 21,450 contracts in fiscal 2026 valued at $6.8 billion in total, a boost from the year prior.
- Military Times, 3 hours ago: US Army showing interest in G/ATOR missile-killing radar, Northrop says.
Northrop Grumman’s new multi-mission radar system has earned high marks from Marine Corps leadership. The U.S. Army has taken notice.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Miss KSA Festival Queen launches ‘The Refinery’ for teen moms.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Miss KSA Festival Queen launches ‘The Refinery’ for teen moms.
Miss Kingston and St Andrew (KSA) Festival Queen Danielle Cox has officially launched her parish project, aimed at addressing the lack of empowerment and access to resources for teenage mothers in her home region. The project, dubbed ‘The Refinery: Becoming, Not Broken’, began in March 2026 at the Mary’s Child Home. According to Cox, who was the second runner-up in the National Festival Queen Coronation in August, not enough is being done to make young mothers aware of opportunities that exits for them.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Ralph, Stewart celebrated for global achievements, commitment to Ja.
MANHATTAN, New York: One conquered Hollywood and Broadway, becoming an Emmy Award-winning actress and humanitarian. The other helped transform a Jamaican hotel company into one of the Caribbean’s most internationally recognised hospitality brands. Last Friday night, their journeys converged at The Plaza in Manhattan, New York, where Sheryl Lee Ralph and Adam Stewart were celebrated at the American Friends of Jamaica’s (AFJ) 45th anniversary Hummingbird Gala for achievements that have carried Jamaica’s influence far beyond its shores.

A deadly Houthi missile attack on a military training camp in Shabwa province killed at least 50 coalition fighters. The attack also resulted in over two dozen troops wounded, according to military officials. Following the strikes, Yemeni forces reported recapturing territory in Taiz governorate, while Houthi forces continued their offensive. In another incident, a coalition airstrike killed nine people, including children and women, in Saada.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Beyond air power: How long-range missiles are reshaping the rules of war.
Long-range precision strikes are increasingly reshaping military operations and strategies across various countries. The focus on missiles and rockets, especially by Pakistan and India, highlights this evolving dynamic. India has enhanced its conventional strike capabilities, while Pakistan has established the Army Rocket Force Command to improve its response options. Both nations are expanding their military arsenals, reflecting the heightening competition.

- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: UN agency to end monthly aid to 500,000 people in Gaza over funding shortfall.
The World Food Programme said Monday it would end monthly assistance to 500,000 people in Gaza due to a funding shortfall, despite acute needs in the war-battered Palestinian territory. With the cutbacks, 1.1 million Palestinians in Gaza — still about half the population — will be receiving either food or cash assistance each month from the UN agency, in reduced amounts. The World Food Programme (WFP) said its efforts had mitigated the effects during a famine last year in Gaza and warned that conditions had not improved to the point that it can take away aid. “People are not safe.
